blocks.text: Jason Jordan has joined Brackenridge Civil Group as a Design Technician. He takes the CAD work on the roadway and site sets, and he keeps the firm's standard details and border sheets current across the active project folders. We are glad to have him.

Jason works in the engineering group and reports to Linda George, Project Engineer. Linda assigns his sheets and sets the order of his work against the project schedule. His first stretch will be on the roadway sets, where the standard details have drifted from the notes that call them and want a careful pass. The roadway and site sheets are the busiest part of the board, and a steady hand on them frees the engineers to design. Site work here is a coordinated effort: the technician holds the set together while the engineer carries the design, and the two are expected to talk through anything that does not square between them.

The practical matters are few. His station is on the CAD network, and the standard-detail library sits under the lettered project folders where the office keeps it. He plots a check print of anything before it leaves his desk. Time is kept by project number on the weekly sheet, and Linda will show him which numbers his hours land against. One rule holds without exception: no sheet leaves this office until the set has been checked and the cover sheet sealed. Where a detail no longer matches the note that calls it, he is to flag it rather than quietly redraw it, so the engineer of record sees the change. When a set calls for it, he may go out to the site with an engineer to check the drawn conditions against the ground; the office would rather he see the site than take the plan on faith. He has already shown the eye we hire for, and a mislabeled contour does not get past him.
His first task is to sit with Linda George and walk the roadway standard set, so the library is square before the next job turns.
